points.text: The image shows the percentage distribution of males and females across age groups from 0–4 to 85+.
It is a horizontal population pyramid, with males shown on the left and females on the right.
The highest shares occur in the 25–34 age group, at 16.2 per cent for males and 16.5 per cent for females.
In the 85+ group, males account for 0.7 per cent and females account for 1.1 per cent.
The percentages generally increase toward the younger and middle-aged groups, peak at 25–34, and then decline among older groups.
Females exceed males in most younger groups, while males exceed females from 35–44 through 65–74; the 75–84 values are equal.
The diagram compares an overshot water wheel and a breastshot water wheel.
Both wheels contain paddles around the rim, spokes, a central hub, water flow arrows, and a tail race.
In the overshot wheel, water enters from a flume above the top of the wheel.
In the breastshot wheel, water enters at about the middle height on the left side of the wheel.
The rotation arrows show the overshot wheel turning clockwise and the breastshot wheel turning anticlockwise.
The two wheel types differ mainly in where water is supplied to the paddles.
The line chart shows the total population of Thorably from 1870 to 2010.
The population generally declined from 1870 to 1950, despite several small fluctuations.
The population reached its highest point in the 1960s, at a level above 300.
The lowest population level occurred in 1950, at roughly 125.
After the sharp peak in the 1960s, the population fell substantially to around 150 by 2000 and remained near that level in 2010.
The line graph shows the number of arrests per year for using illegal drugs from 1991 to 2005.
Arrests increased sharply from 1991 to 1995, remained stable until 1997, and then fluctuated considerably.
The highest number of arrests occurred in 2000, while the lowest occurred in 1991.
The figure reached 60 arrests annually from 1995 through 1997.
After peaking in 2000, arrests dropped sharply in 2001 before rising again in 2002.
By 2005, the number of arrests was higher than at the beginning but lower than the peak.
The line graph shows consumer confidence, indexed to 2002 equals 100, from January 1990 to January 2008.
A single fluctuating line tracks consumer confidence against an index scale ranging from 60 to 110.
Consumer confidence reaches its highest point around 2002, at approximately 105, and its lowest point in the early 1990s, below 70.
The index fluctuates substantially before 2002, remains near 95 to 100 for several years, and then falls sharply after 2007.
Confidence is generally higher during the period from 2002 to 2007 than during most of the 1990s.
Overall, consumer confidence is highly volatile, with a prolonged elevated period followed by a dramatic decline at the end.
The line graph shows the number of laws in Brazil from 1953 to 1993.
The horizontal axis represents years, while the vertical axis measures the number of laws.
The number of laws generally increased throughout the period, with faster growth after the 1970s.
The highest value occurs in 1993, at more than 2,000 laws.
The number remained relatively low in the 1950s and 1960s compared with the sharp rise during the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Overall, Brazil experienced a substantial long-term increase in the number of laws over these four decades.
The line chart shows intraday movements in the S&P/ASX 200 index from 10:00 to 2:00.
The horizontal axis displays time, while the vertical axis marks index levels at 3468, 3484, and 3500.
The index reaches its highest visible level just below the 3500 mark during the late morning.
Overall, the index rises sharply from around 10:00, peaks before midday, and then fluctuates lower through the early afternoon.
The index remains mostly above 3484 after its initial rise, despite several short-term declines.
By the end of the displayed period, the index is below its late-morning peak but above its starting level.
The line graph shows Ontario manufacturing employment and the Canadian dollar exchange rate from 1981 to 2013.
The blue line represents Ontario manufacturing employment in thousands, while the red line represents the Canadian dollar value in US dollars.
Manufacturing employment reaches its highest level at just above 1,100 thousand around 2001–2002, then declines substantially.
The Canadian dollar reaches its lowest level near 0.64 US dollars around 2002 and its highest level near 1.01 around 2011.
After about 2002, the Canadian dollar rises strongly while manufacturing employment generally falls, showing an opposite movement between the two series.
The line graph shows US fruit and vegetable consumption trends in pounds per person per year from 1970 to 2010.
The graph compares two categories: vegetables and fruit.
Vegetable consumption reaches the highest level at about 425 pounds per person per year in the late 1990s.
Vegetable consumption generally rises from the 1970s to the late 1990s, then declines slightly toward 2010.
Vegetable consumption remains higher than fruit consumption throughout the period, with the gap generally widening after 1990.
The line graph shows life expectancy at birth in years for males and females from 1881–1890 to 2011–2013.
The graph compares two series, males and females, across years on the horizontal axis.
Life expectancy increased substantially for both sexes over the period, with a brief plateau around the 1960s and 1970s.
Females consistently had higher life expectancy than males throughout the period.
The highest life expectancy appears for females at the end of the period, while the lowest appears for males at the beginning.
The chart indicates a persistent female advantage and an overall improvement in life expectancy for both sexes.
The line chart compares population growth and growth in rating base from 2012 to 2022, by financial year ending 30 June.
The chart contains two series: population growth shown in blue and growth in rating base shown in light green.
Population growth stays near 1.5% until 2016, then gradually declines to about 1.3% in 2022.
Growth in rating base reaches its highest point at just under 2.0% in 2018.
Rating-base growth rises above population growth around 2017 and remains higher through 2022.
By 2022, rating-base growth is visibly stronger than population growth.
The stacked area chart shows electricity generation in China by type from 1994 to 2004, measured in billion kilowatthours.
The chart compares conventional thermal generation in red with hydroelectric generation in blue.
Total electricity generation rises steadily throughout the period, with faster growth after 2002.
Conventional thermal power remains much larger than hydroelectric power in every year shown.
The highest total electricity generation occurs in 2004, when the stacked total is slightly above 2,000 billion kilowatthours.
The line graph shows the percentage of university and college students doing educational activities by hour on weekdays.
The graph compares full-time students with part-time students from 12 am to 11 pm.
Full-time students reach their highest participation at about 36%, while part-time students peak at about 21%.
Both groups rise sharply during the morning, decline through the afternoon, and fall again after evening.
Full-time students consistently have higher percentages than part-time students for most hours.
Educational activity is generally greatest during late morning and lowest during the early morning and late evening.
The graph shows carbon dioxide concentration and temperature change over the last 400,000 years, with age measured in years before present.
The blue line represents CO2 measured in ppm, while the red line represents temperature change in degrees Celsius relative to the present.
CO2 values fluctuate between approximately 180 and 300 ppm, while temperature change ranges from about -10 to 4 degrees Celsius.
Both variables show repeated rises and falls, with several pronounced peaks followed by extended declines across the period.
The two lines generally move in similar directions, with major high points occurring around 300,000, 200,000, and 120,000 years before present.
The graph indicates a recurring relationship between higher carbon dioxide levels and higher temperatures over geological time.
The line graph compares oil prices in dollars with the food price index from 2000 to 2009.
The graph contains a red oil-price line using the left axis and a green food-price-index line using the right axis.
Both series reach their highest levels around 2007, with oil near $130 and the food price index near 210.
Both measures generally rise over the period, despite fluctuations and a sharp decline around 2008.
After the 2008 drop, the food price index recovers more strongly than oil prices by the end of 2009.
The line graph shows projected population in Australia, measured in millions, from 2001 to 2101 at 30 June.
The graph compares three projections labelled Series A, Series B, and Series C.
The vertical scale ranges from 20 million to 70 million.
All three series increase over time, although Series A rises much more steeply than the other projections.
By 2101, Series A is the highest projection, while Series C is the lowest.
The gap between Series A and Series C becomes considerably wider toward the end of the period.
The line graph shows U.S. energy consumption by fuel from 1980 to 2030, measured in quadrillion units.
It compares petrol and oil, coal, natural gas, nuclear, solar/wind, and hydropower across historical data and projections.
Petrol and oil is the highest fuel source throughout, rising to just under 50 quadrillion units by 2030.
Coal increases from about 16 quadrillion units in 1980 to around 32 by 2030, overtaking natural gas after 2015.
Natural gas levels off at about 25 quadrillion units from 2015 onward, while nuclear and solar/wind remain much lower.
The chart indicates that fossil fuels remain far more important than nuclear, solar/wind, and hydropower through 2030.
The bar chart shows internet population by country, measured in millions of users.
The countries shown are China, the US, Japan, Germany, the UK, France, India, Russia, Brazil, South Korea, Canada, Italy, Spain, Mexico and the Netherlands.
China has the highest internet population, at about 180 million users.
The US is second with about 165 million users, while Japan is a distant third at about 60 million.
After the two leading countries, internet populations decline sharply and then remain below 40 million for most countries.
Mexico and the Netherlands have the smallest internet populations, at roughly 12 million each.
The image shows taxation by countries for payroll and superannuation in recent years.
The listed categories are Australia, Austria, other countries, Denmark, and a weighted average.
Australia and Austria have the highest displayed amounts, tied at 16.6%.
Although Austria is ranked second, its displayed amount is the same as Australia’s.
The horizontal bars generally decrease from the top countries through the middle countries to Denmark.
Denmark has the smallest bar among the named country entries, while the weighted average is shown separately in grey.
The bar chart compares unemployment rates by ethnic group and sex in the UK in 2001, measured as percentages.
It shows nine ethnic groups, with separate horizontal bars for men and women in each group.
Bangladeshi women have the highest visible unemployment rate, at just under 25 percent.
The percentage axis runs from 0 to 30, with gridlines at intervals of 5.
Women have higher unemployment than men in the Mixed, Pakistani and Bangladeshi groups, while men are higher in several other groups.
Unemployment rates vary substantially across ethnic groups, with Bangladeshi and Pakistani groups generally higher than White and Indian groups.
The chart compares unemployment rates and median weekly earnings in 2012 by educational attainment.
The education categories range from less than a high school diploma to doctoral and professional degrees.
Professional degree holders have the highest median weekly earnings, while people without a high school diploma have the lowest earnings and highest unemployment.
Unemployment is lowest for professional degree holders at 2.1%, followed by doctoral degree holders at 2.5%.
Higher educational attainment generally corresponds to higher weekly earnings and lower unemployment rates.
All workers have an unemployment rate of 6.8% and median weekly earnings of $815.
The stacked bar chart shows drinking habits by age in the US, measured as percentages.
The age groups are 16-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64 and 65-74, with categories for never, ex-, light and heavy drinkers.
Each stacked bar reaches 100 on the percentage scale.
Never drinkers are highest among people aged 16-24, at about 62 percent, while ex-drinkers are highest among those aged 65-74, at about 42 percent.
The proportion of never drinkers generally declines with age, while the proportion of ex-drinkers rises sharply in the two oldest groups.
Older people, especially those aged 65-74, are much more likely to be ex-drinkers than younger people.
The pie chart shows kinds of wheat exported from Australia in 2005, measured in tonnes.
The chart includes Durum Wheat, General Purpose Wheat, Australian Hard Wheat, and Organic Wheat.
General Purpose Wheat was the largest export, while Organic Wheat was the smallest.
The export quantities were 25109 tonnes of General Purpose Wheat and 15176 tonnes of Australian Hard Wheat.
Durum Wheat exports exceeded Organic Wheat exports but were lower than Australian Hard Wheat exports.
The pie chart shows the approximate composition of the air by percentage.
The air is divided into nitrogen, oxygen, and other gases.
Nitrogen is the largest component at 79%, while other gases are the smallest at 1%.
Oxygen accounts for 20% of the air.
The chart shows that air consists overwhelmingly of nitrogen, followed by oxygen, with only a small amount of other gases.
The pie chart shows the causes of deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon from 2000 to 2005.
The chart includes cattle ranching, small-scale agriculture, large-scale agriculture, logging, and other causes.
Cattle ranching is the largest cause, accounting for 65-70% of deforestation.
Small-scale agriculture contributes 20-25%, while large-scale agriculture contributes 5-10%.
Logging and other causes are the least significant categories, together accounting for 3-5%.
The image compares the population percentages of European Union countries in 1998 and 2007.
The pie charts show Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, Spain, Poland, and all other countries.
All other countries formed the largest share in both years, rising from 29.4% in 1998 to 29.7% in 2007.
Germany had the largest share among the named countries, but its percentage fell from 17.1% to 16.6%.
France, the United Kingdom, Italy, and Spain increased slightly, while Germany and Poland decreased.
The image compares the relative sizes of several planets, including Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Earth, and Pluto.
Jupiter and Saturn are the two largest planets shown, followed by Uranus and Neptune.
Jupiter is the largest object shown, while Pluto is the smallest labeled object.
Earth is much smaller than the four outer giant planets but larger than Pluto.
The image shows a dramatic decrease in apparent planetary size from Jupiter and Saturn to Earth and Pluto.
The image illustrates correct and incorrect hand and wrist positions when using a computer keyboard and mouse.
The upper section compares correct and incorrect finger and hand placement on a keyboard.
The lower section compares correct and incorrect wrist and hand posture while operating a mouse.
Correct positions keep the hands and wrists aligned, whereas incorrect positions show bent or awkward angles.
The diagram emphasizes maintaining neutral hand and wrist alignment during computer use.
The image is an Adults Healthy BMI Chart showing weight in kilos against height in metres.
The chart contains coloured BMI bands labelled Under Weight, Healthy Weight, Over Weight, Obese, and Extreme Obese.
The horizontal axis shows height labels from 1.36 to 2.00 metres.
The vertical axis shows visible weight labels from 50 to 110 kilos.
All BMI category bands rise toward the right, indicating that higher heights correspond to higher weight ranges.
A person’s BMI category depends on the combination of height and weight shown by the coloured bands.
The diagram titled "How Solar Yard Lights Work" shows an exploded view of a solar yard light and its components.
From top to bottom, the light is assembled from a glass cover, solar cells and photoresistor, a housing, electronic parts, and a lamp cover.
The upper section contains the glass cover, solar cells, and a photoresistor.
The middle section includes a battery, controller board, and LED beneath the main housing.
The lamp cover forms the lower outer section and surrounds the LED assembly.
The illustration shows that the solar yard light combines solar collection, battery power, electronic control, and an LED lamp.
The image shows a food pyramid with food and drink groups arranged in five levels.
From bottom to top, the pyramid shows water, bread and cereals with fruits and vegetables, dairy with meat and fish, and junk food.
The bottom level contains water, while the next level is divided between bread and cereals and fruits and vegetables.
The middle level is divided between milk, cheese and eggs and meat, poultry, sausage and fish.
Junk food, sweets and sugar drinks are placed alone at the smallest top section.
The pyramid visually suggests that water and lower-level food groups form the broadest part of the diet.
The image shows government expenditure on education across all sectors.
The pyramid divides education spending into Early Childhood, Schools, Vocational Educational Training, and Higher Education.
Early Childhood expenditure is shown as $0.8–1.4 billion, while Schools receive $3–4 billion.
Vocational Educational Training receives $2 billion, compared with $1.8 billion for Higher Education.
Schools have the highest displayed sector expenditure at $3–4 billion, while Early Childhood has the lowest range of $0.8–1.4 billion.
The separate Education Investment Fund is labelled as $11 billion, much larger than the displayed sector amounts.
The image shows a floor plan for a library, with five numbered areas and several facilities.
The upper section contains areas 1, 2, and 3, while areas 4 and 5 are positioned below them.
An entrance is located along the lower edge of area 3, leading into a passageway.
The lower-right section includes separate female and male toilets, an elevator, and a marked walkway.
Areas 1, 2, and 4 are visibly larger than the narrower central area 5.
The plan indicates that visitors enter from the upper rooms into a circulation area connected to the toilets and elevator.
The diagram shows how a river meander is cut off to form an oxbow lake in stages A and B.
Stage A shows a winding river meander with a narrow neck between two nearby bends.
In stage B, sand and silt block the ends of the former bend after the river forms a new, straighter channel.
The abandoned loop of water is labelled as an oxbow lake in stage B.
The river flows through the meander in stage A, whereas stage B shows the main flow diverted through the new channel.
The diagram indicates that deposition of sand and silt separates the meander loop from the main river.
The diagram shows the distribution of the world's water, including freshwater and its main components.
Saltwater makes up 97.5% of total global water, while freshwater accounts for only 2.5%.
Total global water is 1,386,000,000 cubic km, and total freshwater is 35,029,000 cubic km.
Glaciers and permanent snow are the largest freshwater store at 68.7%, followed by groundwater at 30.06%.
Ground ice and permafrost account for .86% of freshwater, while other sources represent 1.22%.
Within the small other category, lakes are .26%, whereas rivers and plants or animals are only .006% and .003%.
The diagram titled "Lunar Cycle affect Fish Catch Rates" shows fish positions during four lunar phases.
Each panel shows a yellow moon above blue water, divided into surface and bottom zones.
In the first panel, fish are concentrated near the bottom, while in the final panel they are concentrated near the surface.
Across the sequence, the fish distribution moves from deeper water to more scattered positions and then toward the surface.
The full-moon panel shows the fewest visible fish and the widest spread through the water.
The image suggests that fish catch locations vary according to the lunar cycle.
The image compares computers from the past with a modern desktop computer.
The older computer is a large, bulky cabinet with multiple panels, a small screen, and a built-in keyboard.
The modern computer consists of a separate tower, a large flat-screen monitor, a keyboard, and a mouse.
The older computer occupies much more space, while the modern system has separate, slimmer components.
The image shows that computer design has changed from large integrated cabinets to more streamlined desktop systems.
The image compares the heights of Hemlock, Cedar, Spruce, and Douglas Fir trees in feet.
Four tree types are shown from left to right: Hemlock, Cedar, Spruce, and Douglas Fir.
The displayed heights are 130 feet for Hemlock, 200 feet for Cedar, 230 feet for Spruce, and 280 feet for Douglas Fir.
Douglas Fir is the tallest tree at 280 feet, while Hemlock is the shortest at 130 feet.
Tree height increases steadily from Hemlock through Cedar and Spruce to Douglas Fir.
Douglas Fir is 150 feet taller than Hemlock.
The diagram compares the bone structures of a human arm, seal limb, bird wing, and bat wing.
The human arm labels the hand, wrist and fingers, radius, ulna, and humerus.
All four limbs show corresponding upper-arm, forearm, and digit bones in similar colour-coded positions.
The seal limb has spread digits, while the bird wing has feathers and the bat wing has elongated finger bones supporting a membrane.
The image visibly shows a shared basic bone pattern adapted into different limb shapes.
The image shows a cross-section of Earth’s internal layers and their approximate thicknesses in miles and kilometers.
The diagram identifies the inner core, outer core, mantle, and crust.
The inner core is labeled 800 miles (1,300 kilometers), while the outer core measures 1,400 miles (2,250 kilometers).
The mantle is approximately 1,800 miles (2,900 kilometers) thick, whereas the crust ranges from 5 to 25 miles (8 to 40 kilometers).
points.value: 1,800 miles (2,900 kilometers); 5 to 25 miles (8 to 40 kilometers)

points.text: Among the labeled layers, the mantle is thickest and the crust is by far the thinnest.
The image shows two homemade bird feeders made from plastic bottles and filled with seeds.
Each feeder is a hanging plastic bottle with a string at the top, seed inside, and wooden perches through the sides.
The left feeder has a blue bottle cap and coloured perch ends, while the right feeder has a clear cap and plain wooden perches.
A bird is perched on the right-hand feeder, while the left-hand feeder is shown without a bird.
The two pictures demonstrate that recycled plastic bottles can be used as simple hanging bird feeders.
The diagram titled "Parts of a Tree" labels the main parts of a tree.
The visible labels identify leaves, a twig, a branch, the trunk, roots, and the crown.
Leaves, twigs and branches are shown above ground, while roots are shown below the soil.
The trunk forms the central vertical part, connecting the crown above to the roots below.
The diagram shows that the crown is the upper leafy section of the tree.
The map shows predicted global temperature increases from 2070-2100 compared with the 1960-1990 average.
The world map uses colors from pale yellow to dark red to represent different temperature increases.
The temperature-increase scale ranges from 0 to 8 degrees Celsius.
The highest increases appear over northern South America and parts of the Arctic and northern continents, shown in dark red.
Land areas generally show greater warming than the oceans, which are mostly pale yellow or light orange.
The map indicates that warming is projected to be unevenly distributed across the globe.
The image shows the germination of a bean plant.
The process progresses from a bean seed to a sprouting seed, then a young seedling, and finally a leafy plant.
Each developing stage is shown in soil, with roots growing downward beneath the ground.
As germination proceeds, the roots become larger and more branched while the stem grows upward.
The final plant is much taller than the earlier stages and has several green leaves above the soil.
The diagram shows that a bean seed develops into a mature plant through successive growth stages.
The image illustrates the water cycle across mountains, land, rivers and the sea.
Water evaporates from the sea, is transported by clouds, and falls as precipitation over the mountains.
Blue upward arrows labelled Evaporation rise from the sea toward the clouds.
Precipitation is shown as raindrops falling from clouds over the mountainous area.
Surface run-off flows downhill through the land and returns toward the sea.
The diagram shows that water continually circulates between the ocean, atmosphere and land.
The image shows the Tesco Extra Music Download process.
A central Tesco Extra Music Download panel is surrounded by icons for search, purchase, download and play.
The cycle proceeds from Search to Purchase, then Download, and finally Play.
Search is represented by a magnifying glass, purchase by a shopping cart, download by a downward arrow, and play by headphones.
The diagram presents music downloading as a circular four-step service process.
The diagram shows the fungus gnat lifecycle, which is about 28 days.
The lifecycle progresses from eggs to larva, then pupa, and finally adult.
Eggs develop for 4-6 days before the larval stage.
The larval stage lasts 12-14 days, the longest duration shown.
The pupal stage takes 3-6 days, while the adult stage lasts 7-10 days.
The larval stage occupies the largest part of the fungus gnat lifecycle.
The diagram shows how industrial emissions are transformed in the atmosphere and return as acid deposition.
Industry, transportation, ore smelting, and power generation release nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere.
Atmospheric emissions undergo chemical transformation, producing nitric acid and sulfuric acid before condensation occurs.
The transformed pollutants return through dry fallout of particulates and gases or through precipitation.
Precipitation can include acid rain, fog, snow, and mist, showing that pollutants are deposited in several forms.
The line graph titled "Years to Double Population" shows the years required for population doubling by ending year.
The horizontal axis shows Ending Year, while the vertical axis shows Years to Double.
The longest doubling period was 544 years, from 0.375 to 0.75 Billion, ending in 1715.
Population doubling times declined sharply from 544 years in 1715 to 39 years by 1999.
Later doubling periods were 79 years ending in 1960, 47 years ending in 1974, and 39 years ending in 1999.
A red forecast-only label near 2025 suggests a possible doubling from 4 to 8 Billion.
The line graph shows monthly Dubai gold sales in 2002, measured in millions of Dirhams.
The graph presents gold sales for each month from January to December.
Sales reached their highest point in March at 350 million Dirhams.
The lowest sales figures occurred in July and September, at 120 million Dirhams.
Sales rose from January to March, then generally declined to July before fluctuating for the rest of the year.
After the March peak, monthly gold sales ended the year below the January level.
The diagram shows the Sun, Moon and Earth alignment that produces solar eclipses.
The Sun is on the left, the Moon is positioned between it and the Earth, and Earth is on the right.
Shadow regions behind the Moon are labelled as the umbra and penumbra.
A total eclipse occurs in the narrow umbra, while a partial eclipse occurs in the wider penumbra.
Dashed circular paths around Earth and the Moon are labelled Earth's orbit and Moon's orbit.
The image shows that eclipse type depends on where Earth lies within the Moon's shadow.
The diagram shows how Dell operates a closed-loop plastics supply chain.
The cycle begins with collecting and recycling materials, followed by sorting and shredding.
The next stages are molding and manufacturing, then assembling and shipping products.
The final stage is purchase and use, which returns to collection and recycling in a circular loop.
Icons show a recycling truck, shredder, factory, computer, and customer across the five stages.
The circular arrow indicates that plastics are reused continuously through the supply chain.
The map shows honey production as a percentage of national production by state in Mexico.
Mexico is divided into Northern, Central, and Southern zones, with states shaded by production category.
The legend gives four honey-production ranges: 0–1%, 1–3%, 3–10%, and 10–16.38%.
The highest category is 10–16.38%, represented by the darkest brown shading.
Most northern states are in the lightest production categories, while darker categories are concentrated in central and southeastern areas.
The image compares fish distribution near a rocky seabed during the day and at night.
The picture is divided into two panels labelled DAY on the left and NIGHT on the right.
Four individual fish are visible in the daytime panel.
Nine fish are visible together in the nighttime panel.
At night, the fish form a larger, denser group than during the day.
The image suggests that these fish are more grouped together at night and more dispersed during the day.
The map shows Australian population density in 2011, measured as people per sq km.
Australia is divided into five population-density colour categories, from pale yellow to dark red.
The lowest density category is less than 0.1 people per sq km.
The darkest red areas, representing 100.0 or more people per sq km, occur mainly along parts of the coast.
Population density is generally lowest across the central inland and higher around coastal areas.
The map indicates that Australia’s population was concentrated near the coast rather than in the interior.
The image shows a circular process for handling fruits, illustrated with grapes.
Grapes are shown growing on vines at the top right of the cycle.
The grapes are transported by a pickup truck and then move along a conveyor belt.
The processed grapes are placed into a box before being put into a shopping cart.
Arrows connect all five pictures in a clockwise cycle from growing grapes to shopping for fruit.
The horizontal bar chart shows average weekly household spending on goods and services in 2015-16, measured in dollars.
The chart compares 15 spending categories, including housing, food, transport, recreation, health, education and tobacco products.
Current housing costs for selected dwellings have the highest average weekly household spending, reaching about $250.
Food and non-alcoholic beverages and transport are the next two largest expenses, while recreation is also substantially high.
Tobacco products have the lowest average weekly household spending, at only around $10.
Overall, weekly household spending is concentrated in housing, food and transport, with much smaller amounts spent on the lowest-ranked categories.
The diagram shows how rotation is converted into electricity for homes.
A wind turbine with three rotating blades is connected to an electrical unit at its base.
The turbine rotation produces electricity, which passes through cables from the electrical unit.
Several power lines extend from the unit to multiple houses and a larger building.
The image illustrates wind-generated electricity being distributed to nearby buildings.
The line chart shows population growth in thousands from 1978/1979 to 2008/2009.
It compares total growth, natural increase, and net international migration.
Total growth reaches its highest point at just under 500 thousand around 1988/1989.
Natural increase generally declines from about 200 thousand to around 110 thousand before rising slightly at the end.
Net international migration fluctuates strongly and is higher than natural increase by 2008/2009.
Total population growth falls after its late-1980s peak, then rises steadily to over 400 thousand by the final year.
The stacked bar chart shows the percentage breakdown of electronic and electric waste categories.
Electronic waste includes monitors, televisions, computers and related equipment, and DVD, VCR, CD players, radios and Hi-Fi sets.
Electric waste includes refrigerators and household appliances such as washing machines, dryers, air-conditioners and vacuum cleaners.
Washing machines and other household appliances are the largest category at 30%, while monitors and televisions are the smallest at 10% each.
Computers and related equipment and entertainment players each account for 15%, while refrigerators account for 20%.
Electronic waste and electric waste each make up half of the total bar, or 50%.
The map shows Earth's polar, temperate and tropical climate zones by latitude.
Pink polar zones lie beyond 60 degrees north and south, while yellow temperate zones occupy middle latitudes.
The green tropical zone forms a broad band around the Equator between the temperate zones.
The map marks the Equator, 30 degrees north and south, and 60 degrees north and south.
From the North Pole to the South Pole, the zones occur in the order polar, temperate, tropical, temperate and polar.
Climate zones are arranged in broad east-to-west bands that are generally symmetrical around the Equator.
The image shows a compact residential floor plan measuring 5.40 metres by 6.80 metres.
The plan includes a bedroom, living area, kitchen, bathroom, entrance, and a central hallway.
The horizontal dimension across the top is 5.40 metres.
The vertical dimension along the right side is 6.80 metres.
The dwelling is longer vertically than it is wide horizontally.
The furniture arrangement shows a compact home organized around a central entrance and hallway.
The map shows the distribution of tropical and temperate rainforest in South America.
The legend identifies tropical rainforest in green and temperate rainforest in dark teal.
Tropical rainforest covers a large continuous area across northern South America, especially around Brazil and neighbouring countries.
Temperate rainforest occupies a much smaller, narrow strip along the southern Pacific coast near Chile and Argentina.
Tropical rainforest is far more widespread than temperate rainforest on the map.
